## What

Trail 405, T1: the extractor collects evidence about props from the syntax alone. It decides nothing and emits nothing.

- Per component, in the new crate-internal field `ComponentMapping::body` (`BodyFacts`), read from the component's own function. The function is found through `memo`, `forwardRef` and a factory call's first argument, the same unwrapping the extractor already does.
  - `reads`: the destructured keys of the first parameter (renamed, defaulted or nested), and `props.x` / `props['x']` anywhere in the body. `rest` holds the name of the rest binding.
  - `elements`: every JSX element in source order. The tag kind follows the JSX rule (a lowercase first letter, a dash or a namespace makes it intrinsic; otherwise an identifier or a member path such as `chakra.button`). Attributes keep their source order, so an attribute's place before or after a spread is in the data. A named attribute records the prop its value is, when it is exactly one (a destructured name, `props.x` or `rest.x`). A spread records whether it spreads the props object, the rest binding or something else.
  - `handed_on`: set when the props object or rest is passed whole as a call argument (`useX(props)`), or the props object is spread whole into JSX.
  - A function or class the body declares and then uses as a JSX tag counts as a nested component. Its elements are not recorded on the parent. Callbacks such as `items.map(i => <li/>)` are still recorded.
  - `React.createElement` calls produce no elements.
  - A class component, an alias of another component, or a declaration with no body gets `body: None`.
- Per file, in the new crate-internal field `SourceData::jsx_usages` (added at the lead's request): every JSX element outside the component bodies above (pages, stories, helpers, module-level JSX). Each records its tag in the same form and its attribute names in source order, with spreads marked. Nothing is resolved.
- `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 38 to 39. The golden snapshot is regenerated, and its fixture gains a module-level element so that `jsx_usages` is covered.
- A `cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor` changeset is included because `just semver` requires one: a new private field makes both structs impossible to build with a struct expression outside the crate.

## Evidence

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- nextest on `-p caliper-docgen-core`: exit 0, 1182 passed, 1 skipped.
- `just semver`: exit 0 with the changeset, exit 1 without it.
- 11 new tests in `extractor/body_facts.rs`. On origin/main they fail because the evidence does not exist there. They cover:
  - destructuring with a rename, a default, a nested pattern and a rest binding
  - `props.x` / `props['x']` reads
  - an attribute before and after a spread, a DOM spread, a component spread and an "other" spread
  - `{...props}` and `useX(props)` / `useY(rest)`, plus a negative case
  - tag kinds
  - `forwardRef`, `memo(forwardRef)` and `memo` wrappers
  - two return branches and a ternary or `&&`
  - a nested inline component (its elements stay out of the parent)
  - `createElement` (no elements)
  - a class component (no facts)
  - file usages

  - gate-large
  - checker-default/chakra-only
  - shadcn-ui/apps/v4
  - react-spectrum/packages
  - mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src
  - ant-design/components

  - user+sys, median: 0.66 s on base, 0.68 s on the branch. The noise under this load is larger than the difference.

## Not verified

- The instruction counts are for a whole run, not the structural pass on its own. The extra AST walk runs only for JSX files and for files with components.
- Not collected, by the brief's scope:
  - reads through `const { a } = props` in the body
  - `rest.x` reads in `reads` (they do count as an attribute's prop)
  - name shadowing (`props` rebound in a nested function is still read as the component's props)
  - elements of a nested component that is never used as a tag (they are recorded on the parent)
- In `jsx_usages`, elements inside a nested component that sits within a recorded body are recorded nowhere.
- A component built from an identifier alias (`memo(Card)`) gets `body: None`. Its facts are on `Card`.
- No checker-lane, napi, TS or integration tests were run (the output is unchanged).
